checks.ref:
command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
review="$reports/review-code.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-code stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: Coverage: tasks 3.5 and 5.5 are marked ✅ and M6 claims 'Every other module is ≥ 90%', but the measured raw scores are below the 90% minimum (dateTimeFormatWrapper.ts 88.57%, futureRule.ts 51.59%, futureRuleTokens.ts 50.00%, readZoneRules.ts 59.18%, zoneRulesRelease.ts 50.00%). They pass only after discounting 'Survived, testsCompleted: 0' mutants, and the review's own Mutation section says 'The zero-test numbers for the static core files are not proven kills'. Unverified results cannot be ✅: mark 3.5, 5.5 and these M6 modules ⚠️ and add a finding asking for a confirming run (e.g. the project config with a longer time limit), consistent with how check.ts at 89.74% got ❌/R2.

R1 Fix is harmful as written and its Fix risk is wrong: it says to change FIXED_INSTANT in dateTimeFormatWrapper.clock.test.ts to 2026-11-28T19:47:31.250Z, but the test 'reads the instant the native UTC formatter reports' (lines 106-115) asserts '13:00', which is the case task 5.2 and spec scenario 'A formatter without a date formats the current instant' (zone-rules/spec.md:179-182, current instant 2026-07-15T08:00:00Z → 13:00) require. The change breaks that assertion and removes the required case, yet Fix risk says 'none — test-only'. The fix should add a second instant with non-zero month/day/minute/second/millisecond fields alongside the existing case.

R2 Fix contradicts R5 and tasks.md ('every new or changed file stays under 200 lines'): it adds the new `--compiled` case to check.test.ts (already 294 lines) and only splits 'if that case pushes the file past 300 lines'. It should put the new case in a sibling file, or depend on R5's split.
